correctness.rationale: The circle-unitary symmetry gives w(T)=lambda_max(T+T*)/2 on complex ℓ². The positive geometrically decaying Jacobi matrix is compact; for s,t>0 its simple isolated Perron eigenvalue and positive eigenvector support analytic perturbation. At s=0 the block split is one weight-1 edge plus geometrically scaled four-vertex paths with edges (q²,tq³,q⁴); the quartic λ⁴-(a²+b²+d²)λ²+a²d² gives λ=1 at t=q^{-3}sqrt((1-q⁴)(1-q⁸)). Every s>0 forces λ>1 via principal first-three vertices. Above that budget, endpoint derivatives decrease strictly along the segment into its interior; global strict Hessian positivity follows from the spectral second-derivative formula, since Dv=αv has α=0 at row 0 then direction components vanish at rows 1 and 3. Thus unique strictly positive analytic optimizer and strict convexity in c. At large c, the leading disjoint A and B edges have equal top weight a=q³/(1+q²) at x0=q²/(1+q²). Principal edges bound the optimizer displacement y in a fixed compact interval. The top two-dimensional eigenspace has complementary gap a(1-q⁴); uniform Schur control leaves 2×2 M_y=[[qy,q²/2],[q²/2,-q³y]], whose minimum eigenvalue top branch is a at y*=-(1-q²)/(2(1+q²)). This proves the stated nonuniform-in-q two-term expansions. Independently SymPy verified the quartic zero and M_y eigenvalues and a 160-dimensional Jacobi spectral implementation sampled q=.3,.6,.85 at c/c*=.7,1,1.3,10,1000, confirming phases and asymptotic convergence. These finite checks are not asserted to prove all q,c.
residual_risks: Infinite-dimensional proof relies on standard compact positive Jacobi Perron/Kato perturbation facts; they were reconstructed analytically, not certified in Lean or an external proof assistant.
Finite truncations only corroborate; they are not uniform-in-q or exhaustive over c.
Two-term c-asymptotic is proven for each fixed q∈(0,1), no uniformity at q→0 or q→1.

value.rationale: The already-motivated two-parameter four-periodic geometric shift makes a fixed total coefficient budget s+t=c a natural spectral allocation problem, not an arbitrary finite sample. An exact threshold separating a nonattained open-domain infimum from a unique interior optimizer is a full, nontrivial parametric classification for every q∈(0,1), with rigorous curvature and the sharp order-one displacement of the optimal split as c→∞. The model is compact infinite-dimensional, and the singular two-edge spectral crossing requires specific analysis beyond fixed-parameter determinant evaluation. The result is self-contained and could inform subsequent optimal spectral design calculations for weighted Jacobi operators; no general theorem or paper-sized downstream consequence is required. Its mathematical significance does not depend on uniqueness of wording; remaining priority caveats are in originality.
residual_risks: The objective uses the particular coefficient sum s+t rather than the sum of physical weighted edges; this modeling choice is mathematically natural for the existing modulation parameters but not a universal design principle.
No explicit closed elementary formula for finite-c interior optimizer; value lies in exact phase/uniqueness/asymptotics.

scientific_limitations: Finite numerical tests do not establish infinite-dimensional results; proofs for arbitrary real parameters rest on reconstructed Jacobi and perturbation analysis.
